item.title: Why Are We Sprinting Off The AI Cliff? — Thu Nov 5, 4:00 PM — Springstowne Library
item.description:
This is a a free and open event - we'll watch a video and learn together, then discuss our opinions. You'll come away with a better understanding of AI and develop your own ideas about this transformational technology. AI companies are racing to build systems that can improve themselves, even though they admit that they have zero confidence in being able to control them. Journalist Ezra Klein explains the recent HuggingFace incident, and how this might be a warning shot that the public should pay attention to. Join a friendly, beginner conversation on the current state of AI and where we might be headed. You'll come away with enough information to build your own opinion about AI. No registration required, but if you would like an e-mail reminder you can sign up to receive one.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Sonoma Valley Museum of Art FREE Nov 7-8 Bank of America Museums on Us — Sat Nov 7, 11:00 AM — Sonoma Valley Museum of Art
item.description:
Bank of America cardholders receive free general admission to participating museums nationwide on the first full weekend of each month; this month is November 7-8.
With Thanksgiving and winter just around the corner, the late fall season means just one thing: it’s the perfect time for some indoor fun at your local museum! The Sonoma Valley Museum of Art has exciting exhibits including brand new installation The Real-Life Art History of M. Louise Stanley, an exhibit sponsored by Bank of America that celebrates a unique Bay Area Figurative artist for her wildly imaginative narratives and distinctly female perspective, shaped by her keen observations of everyday life and setting her apart from her male contemporaries. The exhibit features Sanley’s large-scale acrylic paintings, gouache and watercolor works on paper, sculptural objects, sketchbooks, studies, photos, and notes from her personal archives, showing the artist’s perspective across multiple media forms.

item.title: ARTIST RECEPTION Just Around The Corner - Paintings by Bill Gittins — Sat Nov 7, 12:00 PM — Rena Charles Gallery
item.description:
**Meet the Artist Reception** Saturday, November 7th from Noon - 4pm at Rena Charles Gallery located at 439 Healdsburg Ave, Healdsburg.
**Just Around The Corner -** Palette knife paintings by Bill Gittins
Rooted in the landscape of Sonoma County, Bill Gittins paints with an eye for color, movement, and the energy of a passing moment. Working in oil with both brush and palette knife, he finds his subjects close to home: vineyards and rolling hills, country roads and winding trails, weathered barns, coastal bluffs, crashing waves and retreating tides, and skies that shift from drifting clouds to blazing sunsets. These scenes become more than features of the natural world; they invite the eye to wander and the imagination to follow. Like the paths we take in life, his roads and trails lead toward possibilities just out of view, and toward whatever waits around the next bend.
Source: Press Democrat

item.title: Sonoma Valley Museum of Art FREE Nov 7-8 Bank of America Museums on Us — Sun Nov 8, 11:00 AM — Sonoma Valley Museum of Art
item.description:
Bank of America cardholders receive free general admission to participating museums nationwide on the first full weekend of each month; this month is November 7-8.
With Thanksgiving and winter just around the corner, the late fall season means just one thing: it’s the perfect time for some indoor fun at your local museum! The Sonoma Valley Museum of Art has exciting exhibits including brand new installation The Real-Life Art History of M. Louise Stanley, an exhibit sponsored by Bank of America that celebrates a unique Bay Area Figurative artist for her wildly imaginative narratives and distinctly female perspective, shaped by her keen observations of everyday life and setting her apart from her male contemporaries. The exhibit features Sanley’s large-scale acrylic paintings, gouache and watercolor works on paper, sculptural objects, sketchbooks, studies, photos, and notes from her personal archives, showing the artist’s perspective across multiple media forms.

item.description:

Join Hugh McCague as we continue to explore Rosicrucian laws and principles and their creative expression and application for the mastery of life, harmonious living, and service.

item.title: Paint & Sip with Genevieve Elkin — Fri Nov 13, 5:30 PM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join us for a relaxed and social paint & sip evening. You'll be guided step-by-step through painting a scenic view using acrylics, with plenty of room to make it your own.
Whether you follow along or add your own creative twist, the focus is on enjoying the process and having fun. Sip on a beverage, come with friends or meet new ones, and settle into a laid-back night of painting and connection. No experience needed - just show up and create.
Genevieve Elkin was Born and raised in Mill Valley, California and is a multidisciplinary artist now based in Petaluma. She earned a BFA in Illustration from Parsons School of Design and has professionally managed art departments, supporting artists and new media on high-profile projects. Genevieve loves painting, drawing, and exploring ceramics, and enjoys helping students experiment, have fun, and develop their own creative voice.
To learn more:@gennaelkin
